invariants.statement: For an equal correctness contract, prefer the representation, algorithm, bounded state, movement and abstraction requiring the least necessary work; additional compute does not justify unnecessary work.
Externally driven resident growth requires an explicit capacity, budget, bounded window, or explicit resource-exhaustion result.
Portable public execution semantics do not require floating point; fractional semantics require an explicit versioned integer representation and declared rounding behaviour.
Managed storage requires explicit ownership and lifetime; representable meaningful movement requires source, destination, and extent identity.
Logical domain size does not imply proportional resident state when bounded windows, regeneration, compact indices, streaming, or reduction preserve semantics.

For invariant semantics, successful result identity is independent of chunk size, scratch budget, worker count, scheduling, cache shape, CPU family, or optional optimized path; benchmark observations are not correctness identity.

The smallest practical scalar deterministic single-threaded implementation is the semantic reference until evidence earns another path; an optimized path must preserve the result contract, provide material measured benefit under its declared workload, and fall back to the correct simpler path when unavailable or when it loses, while genuine resource or correctness failures remain explicit.

Optimization must choose representation and algorithm, bound resident state, remove unnecessary materialisation/movement and duplicate work, improve locality, then measure before SIMD, threading, topology tuning, or specialized CPU acceleration.

The reference runtime targets ISO C99; core correctness cannot depend on C++, managed runtimes, JIT, garbage collection, exceptions, mandatory threads, mandatory SIMD, compiler-specific language extensions, or direct platform-specific facilities outside explicit boundaries.
RUNE targets CPUs and memory and has no GPU execution contract or planned CUDA, OpenCL, Vulkan Compute, Metal, DirectCompute, WebGPU, or shader-compute backend.

Bounds failure, overflow, impossible alignment, exhausted scratch, insufficient destination capacity, and unsupported capability fail explicitly; RUNE does not silently exceed budgets, wrap invalid extents, or truncate unless truncation is the declared operation.
RUNE does not define browser, HTML, CSS, document, GUI, window, image-format, application, or business semantics; general primitives may support those domains only without absorbing their meaning.

Do not create generic scheduler, executor, allocator, backend, cache, plugin, dependency-injection, or task-graph hierarchies for hypothetical future use; a second real implementation must demonstrate the proposed common abstraction before promotion.

Performance observations bind source revision, workload, compiler/toolchain, build configuration, CPU/platform, memory profile, and measurement method; no benchmark result is universal, and timing alone does not establish a causal hardware mechanism.

Donor mechanisms and tests do not transfer constants, worker counts, memory/cache/tile sizes, source expressions, benchmarks, performance claims, or authority automatically; RUNE-specific justification and compatible licensing are required.
Cheap deterministic state may be recomputed instead of retained or fetched only when the correctness contract is preserved; promotion requires RUNE-specific measurement.

Host pointer/size types do not automatically define portable offsets, counts, serialized fields, or externally visible identities; use explicit versioned widths or another explicit versioned representation.
Plans, requested capabilities, advertised CPU features, cross-compiles, and receipt templates do not prove execution; execution evidence states what actually executed and its evidence class.
Human prose and machine-readable contracts remain separate; contradictions are repository defects and automated agents fail closed and report rather than synthesize a reconciliation.
Prefer a materially smaller implementation only when correctness, safety, portability, readability, and evidence are equivalent; smaller code that weakens those properties does not win.
